newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY MAY CUT 98 INFLATION QUICKER THAN PLANNED.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY MAY CUT 98 INFLATION QUICKER THAN PLANNED.

text.p: Hungary, urged by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to cut its inflation more quickly, may revise its 1998 economic policy plans, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told the daily Magyar Hirlap on Monday.
Medgyessy, who attends the World Economic Forum in Davos, told Magyar Hirlap that he had talks with IMF Deputy Chief Executive Officer Stanley Fisher there.

Stanley recognized the results of Hungary's two-year-old economic stabilisation programme, by which the country substantially reduced its budget and current account deficits, but added that Hungary should reduce inflation more quickly, Medgyessy said.
"Following this, I had the idea that perhaps we should work with alternative inflation plans when we prepare the 1998 budget draft," Medgyessy said.
"One would calculate with the originally planned five percent cut (for 1998), while the other with an even larger reduction," he added.
Hungary cut inflation to 23.6 percent in 1996 from 29.2 percent in 1995 and targets 16 to 18 percent for 1997.
